newsitem.title: PERU: Peru may delay decision on Andean pact membership.
newsitem.headline: Peru may delay decision on Andean pact membership.

text.p: Peru could ask the Andean pact group for a further postponement until the end of this year of its decision on rejoining the trade bloc, a top Industry Ministry source told Reuters Wednesday.

The active countries in the Andean pact -- Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador and Bolivia -- decided last month to give Peru until mid-March to reconsider the terms under which it might return to the group.
"We are studying asking for an extension of the deadline until the end of the year," the Industry Ministry source said.
The postponement could further delay talks between the Andean group and South America's largest customs bloc, Mercosur, on uniting to form a trade group spanning South America.
After the expiry of Peru's deadline, Andean pact members were set to begin technical negotiations with Mercosur members -- Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay -- on forming the single bloc.
Peru, which removed itself from the Andean trade pact in 1992 after disagreeing with proposed tariff schedules, has said it is negotiating its own free-trade pact with Mercosur.
